title: CTO Interview with Dr. Zakir Syed of ClockEdge
gist: ClockEdge CTO Zakir Syed argues clock networks, which can be roughly 30% of total power in high-performance processors, need dedicated SPICE-accurate simulation so teams can trim excess timing margin at advanced nodes. He sees gate-all-around, backside power and AI/HPC perf-per-watt pressure raising the stakes, and expects AI to guide exploration rather than replace physics-based simulation.

insights.claim: Clock distribution can account for roughly 30% of total chip power in high-performance processors, and its networks reach every sequential element in a synchronous SoC.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Clock power is a large lever for power efficiency in AI and HPC chips.
insights.quote: In high-performance processors, clock distribution can account for roughly 30% of total chip power.

insights.claim: Conventional transistor-level simulation of whole clock networks was too computationally expensive for large SoCs, so ClockEdge built simulation specific to clocks, combining SPICE-level accuracy with speed and capacity.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Defines the niche ClockEdge occupies versus general-purpose simulators.
insights.locator: Analyzing the entire network with conventional transistor-level simulation

themes.theme: Margin versus PPA at advanced nodes

insights.claim: At advanced nodes, power-supply noise can shift clock edges and alter relative timing between clock paths, while waveform distortion and duty-cycle changes shrink the usable timing window.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Electrical effects once negligible now erode timing windows, driving demand for finer analysis tools.

insights.claim: Engineers add timing margin to cover uncertainty, but excessive margin costs frequency, power or area; the key question customers ask is how much margin is actually needed.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Reclaiming margin is the commercial pitch: better PPA without silicon risk.
insights.quote: The difficult question is how much of that margin is actually needed.

insights.claim: A design can meet timing constraints and still carry unnecessary buffering, excess clock power or more margin than its electrical behavior requires; meeting timing says nothing about whether performance and power are optimal.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Challenges the 'timing met' sign-off mindset and sets up a market for optimization on top of verification.
insights.quote: Meeting timing requirements tells you that a design satisfies its constraints.
insights.locator: A design may meet its timing constraints

insights.claim: ClockEdge's Veridian platform combines timing, jitter, power and aging analysis on full clock trees and meshes, works with industry-standard design data, and fits alongside existing implementation and sign-off flows.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Fit with existing flows lowers adoption friction versus replacing incumbent EDA tools.

insights.claim: ClockEdge's vHelm links electrical analysis to interactive what-if exploration and Virtual ECOs, letting engineers see effects of changes such as resizing a clock buffer on power, waveform quality and jitter before committing to a physical change.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Moves the product from verification into optimization, expanding the use case.

insights.claim: The shift to gate-all-around transistors at 2nm and beyond, plus backside power delivery, changes electrical characteristics and raises the importance of interaction between transistor behavior, power delivery and clock performance.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Process transitions create new analysis needs for EDA vendors.
insights.locator: I expect the interaction between transistor behavior

insights.claim: AI and HPC performance-per-watt demands, with dynamic operating modes and workloads, make clock efficiency matter more because even small improvements count when designs run near their limits.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: AI silicon demand underpins growth for power-optimization EDA tooling.

insights.claim: Detailed electrical analysis historically sits late in implementation; making it available earlier would let engineers choose clock architecture, buffering and optimization before changes become expensive.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: A 'shift-left' of electrical analysis is the methodology change to monitor.

insights.claim: ClockEdge is investigating machine learning to complement circuit simulation, such as neural-network surrogate models for clock jitter trained against detailed electrical simulations.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Early-stage R&D; no product claim made.

insights.claim: AI will not replace physics-based simulation; its value is guiding design exploration and focusing detailed simulation where it adds most value, since designers must know results reflect actual circuit behavior.
insights.speaker: Zakir Syed
insights.so_what: Argues AI augments rather than displaces incumbent simulation EDA.
insights.quote: I don’t see AI replacing physics-based simulation.
